purpose: The acceptance region for a drawn standing-equivalent sagittal profile (PI, PT, SS, LL, TK, Roussouly type). tools/polypose_manifest.py evaluate_profile() reads it; the sampler must reject any profile that fails it BEFORE rendering, and tools/polypose_invariants.py re-evaluates every manifest row against it (check profile_in_envelope). Every bound names its source and says whether the number was re-read from the source today (verified) or is a transcription from memory (verified=false; the checker prints those in its note, as rom_bound does for the ROM table). Edit a bound only with a citation.

conventions.angles: degrees; PI, PT, SS, LL (L1-S1), TK (T4-T12) as in the cited series; PI = PT + SS (Legaye 1998)
conventions.posture: standing. A supine CT is shifted to standing-equivalent by supine_to_standing before it is compared here; the offset cancels in every delta the checker measures on the volume.
conventions.range_rule: range bounds are mean -/+ 3 SD of the cited asymptomatic series: the population support, not the balanced subset
conventions.balance_rule: balance bounds are the SRS-Schwab grade-0 thresholds: |PI - LL| < 10 and PT < 20 (Schwab 2012). A drawn profile must satisfy BOTH range and balance.
conventions.roussouly_rule: type by sacral slope: SS < 35 -> type 1 or 2; 35 <= SS <= 45 -> type 3; SS > 45 -> type 4 (Roussouly 2005). Type 3AP (anteverted pelvis, Laouissat 2018) is accepted as a type-3 SS band. A type inconsistent with its SS fails.

PI.note: mean -/+ 3 SD of Vialle 2005 (abstract values read 2026-09-23 by the sampling-spec pass)

PT.note: population support; the balance rule below is tighter on the high side

LL.note: standing L1-S1; Yukawa 2017 values as recorded in sampling_spec.json citations

TK.note: T4-T12 standing. Our CTs are FOV-limited to ~T8 down, so the checker compares TK DELTAS on the measured span and this range applies to the drawn full-span TK only

balance._why_these_and_not_schwab: CORRECTED 2026-09-23 after an outside check. Until now this section gated on the SRS-Schwab grade-0 thresholds (|PI - LL| < 10 and PT < 20) and evaluate_profile rejected any profile outside them. Measured against the cohort's own ostk numbers, that rule refuses 397 of 686 plate-sane CTSP ordinary spines -- 57.9 % of REAL, unoperated, asymptomatic-cohort people (the same check over all 709 measured ordinary rows refuses 58.3 %). A rule that calls the majority of a normal population out-of-envelope is a definition of SURGICALLY BALANCED, not a reference range, and using it to reject draws would have halved the bank and biased every synthetic spine toward Schwab grade 0 -- the opposite of covering the whole envelope. The gating bounds below are therefore the 2.5-SD population band of the assembled normative model (sampling_spec.json joint_sagittal_model / rejection_envelope), which refuses 49 of 686 (7.1 %). The Schwab grades are kept as a RECORDED DESCRIPTOR per row (schwab_grade, never gating) so a bank can still be reported by balance grade. Reproduce with tools/polypose_sample.py envelope-vs-cohort.

pi_ll_lo.note: SIGNED: PI - LL, not its absolute value. The population is lordotic-biased (mean -5.4), so the band is asymmetric and an abs() bound is wrong in both directions

pi_ll_hi.source: sardar2022 at 2.5 SD; coincides with the Schwab ++ threshold

pt_lo.note: the anteverted floor; a negative PT is anatomy, not an error

pt_hi.source: sardar2022 PT 12.5 +/- 7.3 at 2.5 SD = 30.8; widened to 35 to hold the cohort's own p95+ (29.4) and Diebo's ASD mean 29.2

pi_ll_mismatch_max.note: LEGACY KEY, kept so an older reader does not crash. evaluate_profile prefers pi_ll_lo/pi_ll_hi when present. The value is the widest |PI - LL| the signed band allows; it is NOT the Schwab threshold any more

pt_max.note: LEGACY KEY; evaluate_profile prefers pt_lo/pt_hi when present

schwab_grades_recorded_not_gating.note: from memory of the classification, not re-read today. Reported per row as schwab_grade; status is always 'n/a' so it can never pass or fail a draw

roussouly.note: SS cut-offs 35 and 45 from memory of Roussouly 2005 (Spine 30(3):346-353); check before verified=1. Types 1 and 2 share the SS band and differ by lordosis shape (apex level, number of lordotic vertebrae), which the checker cannot resolve from SS alone.

tk_ll.note: TK = a*LL + b with residual within k*sd. DISABLED until a regression is transcribed from a source on hand (Berthonnaud 2005 / Vialle 2005 give one); the sampler couples TK to LL by drawing jointly and the checker verifies TK lies in range. The checker reports this rule as n/a, never as pass.

supine_to_standing.note: standing L1-S1 54.8 vs supine 50.2 (n=15). No supine-standing TK offset is on hand: null, applied as 0 and said so in every row (profile.supine_to_standing).

sources.vialle2005: Vialle R, Levassor N, Rillardon L, Templier A, Skalli W, Guigui P. Radiographic analysis of the sagittal alignment and balance of the spine in asymptomatic subjects. J Bone Joint Surg Am 2005;87(2):260-267. PMID 15687145

sources.schwab2012: Schwab F, Ungar B, Blondel B, et al. Scoliosis Research Society-Schwab adult spinal deformity classification: a validation study. Spine 2012;37(12):1077-1082
sources.roussouly2005: Roussouly P, Gollogly S, Berthonnaud E, Dimnet J. Classification of the normal variation in the sagittal alignment of the human lumbar spine and pelvis in the standing position. Spine 2005;30(3):346-353

sources.chevillotte2018: Chevillotte T, Coudert P, Cawley D, et al. Influence of posture on relationships between pelvic parameters and lumbar lordosis. Orthop Traumatol Surg Res 2018;104(5):565-568. PMID 30009961
